title: Treasuries rally as investors seek shelter from AI turbulence
key_facts: On Thursday 15 Oct 2026 the 10-year US Treasury yield fell roughly 15 basis points to about 5.04%, its lowest since 23 Sep and a third straight daily decline.
The 2-year yield briefly dropped below 4.69%; the 30-year fell about 12 basis points.
The rally came although US September producer prices rose at the fastest monthly pace in over four years.
Some CoreWeave bonds yield above 15% to 16%, and credit default swap spreads for Oracle and SoftBank widened sharply.
BlackRock this week cut US equities to neutral and raised its view on US Treasuries.
TD Securities strategist Prashant Newnaha called the move 'highly counterintuitive'; stocks and bonds are moving in opposite directions again.
September CPI rose 0.6% on the month, with annual inflation at 3.7%; odds of an October Fed hike rose to about 40%.
quote_evidence: The 10-year Treasury yield briefly dipped to around 5.04%, down roughly 15 basis points on the day, hitting its lowest level since September 23 and marking a third consecutive session of declines.

BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, this week downgraded US equities to "neutral," citing rising AI-related volatility as one reason, while upgrading its view on US Treasuries and expressing a preference for short-duration bonds.
Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities, described the move as "highly counterintuitive."
why_it_matters_hint: Fear about AI financing is pushing money into government bonds despite hot inflation.
